modules.name: Health in an Australian and global context

dots.t: Analyse the current health status of Australians from Australia’s Health and other health reports, tables and graphs
sub: what does the data tell us?
what are the major causes of morbidity and mortality, and the life expectancy for males, females and the general population?
what are the sociological causes of risky health behaviours?
where do inequities exist and what can we do about them?

dots.t: Analyse groups experiencing inequities in health, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and one other group (socioeconomically disadvantaged people, rural and remote, culturally and linguistically diverse populations, people with disability or older people)
sub: what does the data tell us?
how do the determinants interact to affect the health of population groups?
what are some of the causes that underpin the inequities in health?
what actions can be implemented to improve the health status of these groups?

dots.t: Compare the health status of Australia with that of other OECD countries
sub: where does Australia rank in relation to other OECD countries?
why might this be the case?
why do some countries rank higher or lower than Australia?
what can we learn from other countries that may be applied to the Australian context?

dots.t: Examine cardiovascular disease, cancer and ONE other condition in Australia using Australia’s Health and other health reports
sub: what does the data tell us about the mortality and morbidity, prevalence and incidence rates of these conditions?
what are the risk and protective factors for these conditions?
where and for whom are these conditions changing?

dots.t: Investigate the impact of an ageing population on Australia’s health
sub: what does the data tell us?
what is healthy ageing?
what are the opportunities and challenges for an ageing population?
what are current and future strategies to support healthy ageing?
what do government and non-government agencies need to consider to address the future needs of a growing and ageing population?

groups.h: How does Australia’s healthcare system work towards achieving better health for all Australians?

dots.t: Assess the effectiveness of the healthcare system in Australia
sub: the role of the healthcare system
equity of access to the healthcare system
future opportunities for the healthcare system

dots.t: Explain how government and non-government organisations share responsibility for the health system
sub: federal, state and territory and local government
non-government sector – private and not-for-profit

dots.t: Outline how government and non-government organisations collaborate to provide person-centred healthcare
Discuss health expenditure and its impact on current and future populations
sub: healthcare versus prevention
sustainability, access and equity
Medicare, private health insurance and related Commonwealth-funded programs

dots.t: Explain complementary healthcare approaches
sub: products and services available
as a preventative measure
treating the health issue
as a supplement to other medical treatments

dots.t: Explain the importance of being a critical health consumer
sub: how do you know whom to believe?
what do you need to know to make informed decisions?
how do you assess the accuracy and credibility of health information, products and services?

dots.t: Investigate the current and emerging changes and challenges to the healthcare system

groups.h: How is the growing and changing use of technology and data impacting Australia’s healthcare system?

dots.t: Discuss the relationship between technology and health
Investigate new technologies and treatments in the healthcare system
Evaluate the impact of digital health on the healthcare system
sub: what is digital heath?
what services exist?
to what extent has digital health been successful in connecting health information?
what challenges and opportunities does digital health provide for individuals and organisations?

dots.t: Examine how big data is shaping the health of Australians
sub: how is it being used?
how is it reducing healthcare spending?
how is it being used to cure and manage diseases?
what measures need to be taken to ensure privacy and confidentiality of personal information?

groups.h: What actions are needed to promote and improve the health of Australians?

dots.t: Describe the key features of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
sub: SDG 3: Good Health and Wellbeing
SDG 4: Quality Education
SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities
SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities

dots.t: Evaluate the application of SDGs 3, 4, 10 and 11 to inform strategies to improve the health status of a community
sub: how have these goals been applied in other communities?
what lessons can be drawn from other communities and applied to their own community context?
what are the major health issues for a community?
what strategies are needed to advocate and improve a community’s health status?
how do you know these strategies may be effective?

groups.h: How can exercise assessment and prescription be personalised?

dots.t: Explain the importance of using a pre-exercise questionnaire and undertaking relevant health screening by exercise and fitness professionals
Discuss the use of performance/fitness testing for recreational participants and elite athletes to improve their health, participation and performance
Explain how exercise assessment can assist in developing training programs

groups.h: How does training influence movement and performance?

dots.t: Assess the types of training and training methods and their relevance for a variety of sports
sub: anaerobic training, including anaerobic interval, High Intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Sprint Interval Training (SIT), plyometric, and resistance training
aerobic training, including continuous, fartlek, aerobic interval, and circuit training
flexibility training, including static, dynamic, ballistic, and Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF)
strength training, including free/fixed weights, body weight exercises and elastics
skill and tactical development, including drills, modified games and games for specific outcomes

dots.t: Evaluate the application of the principles of training to both aerobic and strength training
sub: progressive overload
training thresholds
reversibility
specificity
variety
warm-up and cool-down

dots.t: Examine the relationship between the principles of training, physiological adaptations and improved performance
sub: heart rate
stroke volume and cardiac output
oxygen uptake and lung capacity
haemoglobin level
muscle hypertrophy
fast/slow twitch muscle fibres

groups.h: How does training differ for individual and group sports?

dots.t: Compare aspects that need to be considered when designing a training session for individual and group sports
sub: health and safety considerations
overview/aim of the session (goal specific)
warm-up and cool-down
skill instruction and practice
conditioning
strategies and tactics
athlete reflection and/or coach evaluation

dots.t: Compare a yearly training program for an individual and a group sport
sub: phases of competition: pre-season, in-season and off-season
sub-phases
peaking and tapering
sport-specific attributes: fitness components, skill requirements

dots.t: Investigate how individual and group sports apply psychological strategies, optimising arousal and management of stress and anxiety, to improve participation and performance
Discuss the factors that influence how strategies and tactics are applied to individual and group sports

groups.h: What impact does sleep, nutrition and supplementation have on movement and performance?

dots.t: Using research, analyse the dietary requirements, pre, during and post performance needed and fluid intake requirements of athletes from different sports
Explain how sleep, nutrition and hydration can be used to reduce fatigue and positively influence movement and injury prevention
sub: guidelines
planning
routines
monitoring

dots.t: Discuss the use of supplements, micronutrients, protein, caffeine and creatine products for improved performance

groups.h: How do individuals train for sustained movement and performance?

dots.t: Explain how biomechanics can be used to develop efficient movements for sustained movement and improved performance
Justify recovery strategies used for sustained movement and performance
sub: physiological, including cool-down, hydrotherapy
psychological, including relaxation

dots.t: Examine the role technology can play to improve performance
sub: training innovations
equipment advances
recording and monitoring training and performance

dots.t: Explain the management and prevention of sporting injuries
sub: classification of sports injuries, including direct and indirect, soft and hard tissue or overuse
assessment of injuries, including the Talk, Observe, Touch, Active movement, Passive movement, Skill (TOTAPS) test
management of injuries
rehabilitation procedures, including progressive mobilisation, graduated exercise, training, use of heat and cold
return-to-play policy and procedures, including application to different sports, responsibility

dots.t: Discuss the impact of drug use on injury management and improving performance
sub: health implications
ethical considerations
drug testing
